title: Operator upgrade fallback strategy and customer escalation playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers on Private/VPC deployments experienced operator crashloops and degraded inference throughput after a Helm-driven operator rollout. Root cause: a regression in the CRD conversion/upgrade hook combined with an annotation mismatch check that caused the KV cache schema migration to skip certain tenant namespaces. Consequences: operator began reconciling partial state, NodeAgent pods were intermittently restarted, and tenants saw increased latency and sporadic 503s. Scope: affects private clusters running operator 3.4.0 upgraded via Helm post-upgrade hooks with older CRD versions present. Goals: stabilize customer clusters quickly, ship a minimal safe hotfix, and implement a safer upgrade path + runbook to avoid recurrence.
acceptance_criteria: operator-3.4.1 hotfix released to Hosted and Private registries
automated preflight hook added to Helm chart that fails safe and prevents upgrade when CRD conversion anomalies detected
customer runbook published with rollback commands and traffic-mitigation steps
at least two affected customer clusters validated in a canary rollout without data loss
post-release monitoring dashboards show error rate and restart rate back to baseline for all targeted tenants
steps_taken: 2026-03-09 22:10 - Incident opened by SRE after support alerts from two enterprise tenants
Created temporary alert suppression to avoid paging for noisy restarts (linked PR for alert gating)
Implement safe-migration flag and preflight dry-run: operator will detect conversion mismatches and skip destructive in-place migration
Added Helm pre-upgrade validator hook and a selectable per-tenant canary label to sequenced rollouts
QA: ran the hotfix against two onprem staging clusters with seeded CRD mismatch cases (results attached to CI run: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/operator-hotfix/245)
2026-03-13 03:40 - Released operator-3.4.1 to private registry and published Helm chart version 3.4.1-hotfix
Customer comms: support sent targeted mitigation steps and offered immediate rollback or guided upgrade; two customers accepted rollback and one accepted canary upgrade
timeline: 2026-03-09 - First customer alert of increased inference errors post-upgrade
2026-03-10 - Full incident triage; created ticket ENG-386702
2026-03-11 - Root cause analysis shows CRD conversion path regression + annotation mismatch
2026-03-12 - Hotfix implementation and internal review (security sign-off not required for minimal change)
2026-03-13 - Hotfix release and phased customer rollouts
2026-03-14 - Post-release monitoring and follow-ups; begin writing permanent upgrade policy
notes: Decision: avoid an automatic in-place CRD migration that mutates tenant resources without explicit opt-in; risk of subtle data/kv loss is too high.
Trade-off: delayed full automated migration increases manual work for some customers but preserves safety. Plan to add an assisted migration tool with strong idempotency guarantees in Q2.
We experimented with automatic schema repair in staging, but observed flaky reconciliation windows causing NodeAgent restarts; reverted that path for the hotfix
Longer-term: implement a declarative upgrade coordinator that sequences conversion and NodeAgent restarts per-tenant with backoff and safe checkpoints
